knowledge:
- key_parameters: data_type=Specifies whether the response column represents "viability" or "inhibition" ;; impute=Logical value indicating whether to impute missing values using the mice package ;; noise=Logical value indicating whether to add small random noise to response values to avoid exact duplicates ;; correct_baseline=Baseline correction method, which can be "non" (no correction), "part" (adjust negative values only), or "all" (adjust all values) ;; method=Vector of synergy reference models to calculate, including "ZIP", "HSA", "Bliss", and "Loewe" ;; iteration=Number of bootstrap iterations to run when analyzing datasets with replicates ;; plot_block=The block ID to extract and visualize from the reshaped dataset ;; plot_value=The metric to plot, such as "response", "response_origin", or model-specific synergy scores (e.g., "ZIP_synergy") ;; dynamic=Logical value indicating whether to generate interactive plotly plots instead of static ggplot/recorded plots ;; distance_method=The distance metric used for dimension reduction in higher-order drug combination visualization (default is "mahalanobis")
- alternatives: mice=Used internally for missing value imputation ;; vegdist=From the vegan package, used internally to calculate distance matrices for higher-order dimension reduction ;; synergyfinderplus.org=A web server implementation of the package providing additional drug and cell line annotations
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing high-throughput pre-clinical drug combination screening datasets (either two-drug or higher-order combinations) to quantify, statistically evaluate, and visualize drug-drug interactions and combination sensitivity.
- pitfalls: Negative readouts in dose-response data can introduce technical errors; use the `correct_baseline` parameter to adjust them closer to 0. Exact duplicate response values can cause errors during curve fitting; set `noise = TRUE` in `ReshapeData` to prevent this. Ensure each block contains at least three concentrations for each drug to calculate sensible synergy scores. Duplicated concentration combinations within the same block ID are automatically treated as replicates; ensure block IDs are correctly assigned.

workflows.name: two_drug_without_replicates
workflows.intent: Analyze and visualize synergy and sensitivity for two-drug combinations without replicates.
input: drug_screening_data.csv (A table containing columns for block_id, drug1, drug2, conc1, conc2, response, and conc_unit)
workflows.stages: 1. Reshape and pre-process the input data using ReshapeData ;; 2. Calculate synergy scores for multiple reference models using CalculateSynergy ;; 3. Calculate sensitivity scores (IC50, RI, CSS) using CalculateSensitivity ;; 4. Visualize dose-response curves, heatmaps, 2D contours, synergy barometers, and synergy-sensitivity plots.
workflows.code:
res <- ReshapeData(
  data = mathews_screening_data,
  data_type = "viability",
  impute = TRUE,
  impute_method = NULL,
  noise = TRUE,
  seed = 1)

res <- CalculateSynergy(
  data = res,
  method = c("ZIP", "HSA", "Bliss", "Loewe"),
  Emin = NA,
  Emax = NA,
  correct_baseline = "non")

res <- CalculateSensitivity(
  data = res,
  correct_baseline = "non"
)

for (i in c(1, 2)){
  PlotDoseResponseCurve(
    data = res,
    plot_block = 1,
    drug_index = i,
    plot_new = FALSE,
    record_plot = FALSE
  )
}

Plot2DrugHeatmap(
    data = res,
    plot_block = 1,
    drugs = c(1, 2),
    plot_value = "response",
    dynamic = FALSE,
    summary_statistic = c("mean",  "median")
  )

Plot2DrugContour(
    data = res,
    plot_block = 1,
    drugs = c(1, 2),
    plot_value = "response",
    dynamic = FALSE,
    summary_statistic = c("mean", "median")
  )

PlotBarometer(
  data = res,
  plot_block = 1,
  plot_concs = c(9.7656, 50), 
  needle_text_offset = 2.5
)

PlotMultiDrugBar(
  data = res,
  plot_block = 1,
  plot_value = c("response", "ZIP_synergy", "Loewe_synergy", "HSA_synergy", "Bliss_synergy"),
  sort_by = "response",
  highlight_row = c(9.7656, 50),
  highlight_label_size = 8
)

PlotSensitivitySynergy(
  data = res,
  plot_synergy = "ZIP",
  show_labels = TRUE,
  dynamic = FALSE
)

workflows.name: two_drug_with_replicates
workflows.intent: Analyze and visualize drug combinations with replicates using bootstrapping to estimate confidence intervals and p-values.
input: drug_screening_replicates.csv (A table containing drug combination screening data with multiple rows per concentration combination within a block)
workflows.stages: 1. Reshape and pre-process data with bootstrapping using ReshapeData ;; 2. Calculate synergy scores with bootstrapping using CalculateSynergy ;; 3. Calculate sensitivity scores with bootstrapping using CalculateSensitivity ;; 4. Visualize response and synergy statistics (SEM, CI) using Plot2DrugHeatmap.
workflows.code:
res <- ReshapeData(
  data = ONEIL_screening_data,
  data_type = "inhibition",
  impute = TRUE,
  impute_method = NULL,
  noise = TRUE,
  iteration = 10,
  seed = 1
)

res <- CalculateSynergy(
  data = res,
  method = c("ZIP", "HSA", "Bliss", "Loewe"),
  Emin = NA,
  Emax = NA,
  correct_baseline = "non",
  iteration = 10
)

res <- CalculateSensitivity(
  data = res,
  correct_baseline = "non",
  iteration = 10
)

Plot2DrugHeatmap(
    data = res,
    plot_block = 1,
    drugs = c(1, 2),
    plot_value = "response",
    dynamic = FALSE,
    statistic = "sem",
    summary_statistic = c("mean",  "median")
  )

Plot2DrugHeatmap(
    data = res,
    plot_block = 1,
    drugs = c(1, 2),
    plot_value = "ZIP_synergy",
    statistic = "ci",
    dynamic = FALSE,
    summary_statistic = c("quantile_25", "quantile_75")
  )

workflows.name: higher_order_combinations
workflows.intent: Analyze and visualize higher-order drug combinations (3 or more drugs) using dimension reduction.
input: higher_order_screening_data.csv (A table containing columns for block_id, drug1, drug2, drug3, conc1, conc2, conc3, response, and concentration units)
workflows.stages: 1. Reshape and pre-process higher-order data using ReshapeData ;; 2. Calculate multi-drug synergy scores using CalculateSynergy ;; 3. Calculate multi-drug sensitivity scores using CalculateSensitivity ;; 4. Visualize high-dimensional landscapes using PlotMultiDrugSurface.
workflows.code:
res <- ReshapeData(
  data = NCATS_screening_data,
  data_type = "inhibition",
  impute = TRUE,
  impute_method = NULL,
  noise = TRUE,
  seed = 1
)

res <- CalculateSynergy(
  data = res,
  method = c("ZIP", "HSA", "Bliss", "Loewe"),
  Emin = NA,
  Emax = NA,
  correct_baseline = "non")

res <- CalculateSensitivity(
  data = res,
  correct_baseline = "non"
)

PlotMultiDrugSurface(
  data = res,
  plot_block = 2,
  plot_value = "response",
  summary_statistic = NULL,
  distance_method = "mahalanobis",
  show_data_points = TRUE
)

PlotMultiDrugSurface(
  data = res,
  plot_block = 1,
  plot_value = "ZIP_synergy",
  summary_statistic = NULL,
  distance_method = "mahalanobis",
  show_data_points = FALSE
)
